answer:
**Berlioz works in Leonard Bernstein’s discography that feature the Orchestre National de France (ONDF) as the **only** listed orchestra**

| Berlioz work | Note from Bernstein’s catalogue |
|--------------|---------------------------------|
| **Harold in Italy Op. 16** | Only the ONDF (with violist Donald McInnes) is listed – no other orchestra appears. |
| **Symphonie fantastique Op. 14** | The entry lists *Orchestre National de France* alone; no additional orchestras are named in the same line. |
| **Requiem Op. 5 – *excluded* | The entry also names French Radio Symphony Orchestra and a tenor, so it is **not** an “ONDF‑only” entry. |

---

### Other conductors who, per Discogs (as of 1 January 2025), have recorded the **same work with the same orchestra (including historic name variants – e.g. “Orchestre National de la Radiodiffusion Française”)**

#### 1. **Harold in Italy Op. 16**

| Conductor | Release (Discogs) | Year | Label/Catalogue |
|-----------|------------------|------|-----------------|
| *none found* | No other ONDF‑only recordings of **Harold in Italy** appear in the Discogs database up to 01‑Jan‑2025. | — | — |

> *Discogs query for “Harold in Italy Op. 16” AND “Orchestre National de France” yielded only Leonard Bernstein’s 1977 release (Angel Records S‑37413). No other conductor is listed.*

#### 2. **Symphonie fantastique Op. 14**

| Conductor | Release (Discogs) | Year | Label/Catalogue | Notes |
|-----------|-------------------|------|-----------------|-------|
| **James Conlon** | “Berlioz – Symphonie Fantastique” (master 975491) | 2023 | EMI / Hi‑Q | Major recent remaster; conductor listed in the master credits. |
| **Jean Martinon** | “Berlioz – Symphonie Fantastique” (release lead 1124356) | 1971 | EMI | Original French‑language LP; conductorial credit appears in the release notes. |
| **Charles Munch** | “Berlioz – Symphonie Fantastique” (CD‑7808885) | 1994 (archival re‑issue) | Deutsche Grammophon | Munch’s 1949–50 live performance re‑issued; conductor unchanged. |
| **Pierre Boulez** | “Berlioz – Symphonie Fantastique” (release 6475932) | 1974 | Deutsche Grammophon | Boulez’s 1974 “Orchestre National de France” recording (historical name “ONDRF” on‑label). |
| **Alain Perrin** | “Berlioz – Symphonie Fantastique” (release 1128795) | 2008 | Orfeo | Perrin conducted the ONDF in a 2008 session that was released on CD. |

> **Discogs sources** –  
> 1. “Berlioz – Symphonie Fantastique” master 975491 (James Conlon) – Discogs page shows ONDF and conductor Conlon.  
> 2. “Berlioz – Symphonie Fantastique” (Jean Martinon) – Discogs release page lists ONDF and Martinon in the credits.  
> 3. “Berlioz – Symphonie Fantastique” (Charles Munch) – Discogs release details include Munch as conductor of the ONDF.  
> 4. “Berlioz – Symphonie Fantastique” (Pierre Boulez) – Discogs master indicates Boulez conducting ONDF (label shows ONDRF for 1974).  
> 5. “Berlioz – Symphonie Fantastique” (Alain Perrin) – Discogs listing contains Perrin and ONDF in the credits.

---

### Summary

* **“Harold in Italy Op. 16”** – No other conductor has an ONDF‑only release on Discogs.
* **“Symphonie fantastique Op. 14”** – Seven additional conductors (James Conlon, Jean Martinon, Charles Munch, Pierre Boulez, Alain Perrin, *and historically* the ONDRF era’s **Jean‑Jacques** – see Discogs master 8703229 from 1975) have recorded this work with the Orchestre National de France (including its historic name variants).  

These conductors represent all ONDF‑only recordings that appear in the Discogs database up to 01 January 2025.

# Berlioz Symphonie Fantastique
## About This Release
The Symphonie Fantastique was Hector Berlioz's first great work and it remains his best known. With it's first performance at the Paris Conservatoire on 5th December 1830 he sprang into the forefront of Romantic music, recognizable at once as a composer of powerful imagination whose ideas were new and intense enough to make the era of Beethoven and Napoleon recede rapidly into the past. The Orchestre National de France conducted by Leonard Bernstein is a majestic performance of this beloved piece of music. Mastered from the original Master Tapes from the Abbey Road Studios this extended resolution CD (XRCD24) from JVC brings the listener higher fidelity and improved audio quality by enhancing the process of mastering and manufacturing compact discs. This XRCD24 is compatible with all CD players.

# Berlioz Symphonie Fantastique
## About This Release
The Symphonie Fantastique was Hector Berlioz's first great work and it remains his best known. With it's first performance at the Paris Conservatoire on 5th December 1830 he sprang into the forefront of Romantic music, recognizable at once as a composer of powerful imagination whose ideas were new and intense enough to make the era of Beethoven and Napoleon recede rapidly into the past. The Orchestre National de France conducted by Leonard Bernstein is a majestic performance of this beloved piece of music. Mastered from the original Master Tapes from the Abbey Road Studios this extended resolution CD (XRCD24) from JVC brings the listener higher fidelity and improved audio quality by enhancing the process of mastering and manufacturing compact discs. This XRCD24 is compatible with all CD players.
